Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in community, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of acts of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.
Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a main pillar in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.
At the level of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Region, is essentially one implementation of the administration of concurrent government affairs which is the authority of the Sumedang Regency Region in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
The Policy on Empowerment and Protection of Women, Child Protection, and Improvement of Family Quality in the Sumedang Regency Region is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Region from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated manner, continuously, and sustainably, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of empowerment and protection of women, child protection, and improvement of family quality.
To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection and to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Region, it must be regulated and stipulated by a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL
Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in community, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of acts of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.
Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a main pillar in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.
At the level of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Region, is essentially one implementation of the administration of concurrent government affairs which is the authority of the Sumedang Regency Region in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
The Policy on Empowerment and Protection of Women, Child Protection, and Improvement of Family Quality in the Sumedang Regency Region is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Region from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated manner, continuously, and sustainably, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of empowerment and protection of women, child protection, and improvement of family quality.
To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection and to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Region, it must be regulated and stipulated by a Regional Regulation.

Part Two Obligations and Responsibilities
Article 51
(1) The Regency Regional Government, the Community, the Family, and Parents or Guardians are obliged and responsible for the administration of Child Protection in the Regency.
(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the Regency Regional Government in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. respecting the fulfillment of Children's Rights without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, group, sex, ethnic origin, culture and language, legal status, birth order, and physical and/or mental condition;
b. implementing and supporting national policies in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency; and
c. providing support for facilities, infrastructure, and the availability of human resources in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency.
(3) The Regency Regional Government, in carrying out its obligations and responsibilities in Child Protection in the Regency as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall do so by:
a. guaranteeing the protection, care, and welfare of Children by taking into account the rights and obligations of Parents, Guardians, or other persons who are legally responsible for Children; and
b. supervising the administration of Child Protection in the Regency.

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in community, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of acts of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.
Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a main pillar in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.
At the level of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Region, is essentially one implementation of the administration of concurrent government affairs which is the authority of the Sumedang Regency Region in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
The Policy on Empowerment and Protection of Women, Child Protection, and Improvement of Family Quality in the Sumedang Regency Region is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Region from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated manner, continuously, and sustainably, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of empowerment and protection of women, child protection, and improvement of family quality.
To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection and to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Region, it must be regulated and stipulated by a Regional Regulation.

Part Two Obligations and Responsibilities
Article 51
(1) The Regency Regional Government, the Community, the Family, and Parents or Guardians are obliged and responsible for the administration of Child Protection in the Regency.
(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the Regency Regional Government in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. respecting the fulfillment of Children's Rights without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, group, sex, ethnic origin, culture and language, legal status, birth order, and physical and/or mental condition;
b. implementing and supporting national policies in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency; and
c. providing support for facilities, infrastructure, and the availability of human resources in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency.
(3) The Regency Regional Government, in carrying out its obligations and responsibilities in Child Protection in the Regency as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall do so by:
a. guaranteeing the protection, care, and welfare of Children by taking into account the rights and obligations of Parents, Guardians, or other persons who are legally responsible for Children; and
b. supervising the administration of Child Protection in the Regency.

Article 70

a. prevention of KTA involving parties in the Regency Area;
b. provision of services for AMPK requiring coordination in the Regency Area; and
c. strengthening and development of Service Provider Institutions for AMPK in the Regency Area.

Article 72

a. development and strengthening of institutional framework for KTA prevention;

c. coordination and synchronization of KTA prevention in the Regency Region.

c. strengthening and development of Women's Protection Service Provider Institutions in the Regency Area.

CHAPTER VIII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 97
(1) The community may participate in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Regency Area.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by:
a. individual Indonesian Citizens;
b. community groups; and/or
c. Community Organizations.
(3) Community Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be facilitated by the Regency Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(4) Facilitation in Community Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be by establishing public participation forums for the welfare of women and Children, Puspaga, community-based integrated child protection, Children's Forum, federation of women's organizations, sekoper cinta, and women heads of households in the Regency Area.
(5) Further provisions regarding Community Participation and Community Participation Facilities in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated in Regent Regulation.

b. third parties; and/or

(5) Regional cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented based on laws and regulations governing regional cooperation.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Part One Definitions
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data according to sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and fulfilling their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self, resulting in, or likely to result in, physical, psychological, and sexual harm or suffering to women and children, including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal actions, and other actions to ensure Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, family environment rights and alternative care, basic health rights and welfare, as well as education rights, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Article 62 Paragraph (1)
Letter a What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disrupts the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.
Letter b What is meant by "Children in Contact with the Law" are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who become victims of criminal acts, and Children who become witnesses to criminal acts.
Letter c What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are in underdeveloped, frontier, and outermost areas in an environment with cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, and religions different from other children, whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.
Letter d What is meant by "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" are Children who become victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.
What is meant by "Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through the Child's sexual organs or other organs of the Child, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecent acts.
Letter e What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.
Letter f What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Pornography" are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.
Letter g What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.
Letter h What is meant by "Child Victims of Kidnapping" are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Selling" are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to other parties for compensation or other reasons.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Trafficking" are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, thereby obtaining consent from a person who holds control over another person, whether conducted within the country or internationally, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.

Letter j What is meant by "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" are Children who experience forced sexual relations, forced sexual relations in unnatural and/or unwanted ways, and forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
Letter k What is meant by "Child Victims of Terrorism Network" are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by terrorism crimes whether as a Child victim, a Child perpetrator, a Child of a perpetrator, and a Child witness.

Letter n What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.
What is meant by Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm to the Child's growth and development process.

Part One Definitions
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data according to sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and fulfilling their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self, resulting in, or likely to result in, physical, psychological, and sexual harm or suffering to women and children, including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal actions, and other actions to ensure Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, family environment rights and alternative care, basic health rights and welfare, as well as education rights, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Paragraph 2
Prevention of Violence Against Women Involving the Parties in the Regency Area

I. GENERAL
Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in community, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of acts of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.
Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a main pillar in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.
At the level of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Region, is essentially one implementation of the administration of concurrent government affairs which is the authority of the Sumedang Regency Region in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
The Policy on Empowerment and Protection of Women, Child Protection, and Improvement of Family Quality in the Sumedang Regency Region is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Region from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated manner, continuously, and sustainably, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of empowerment and protection of women, child protection, and improvement of family quality.
To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection and to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Region, it must be regulated and stipulated by a Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Part One Definitions
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data according to sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and fulfilling their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self, resulting in, or likely to result in, physical, psychological, and sexual harm or suffering to women and children, including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal actions, and other actions to ensure Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, family environment rights and alternative care, basic health rights and welfare, as well as education rights, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Letter a What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disrupts the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.
Letter b What is meant by "Children in Contact with the Law" are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who become victims of criminal acts, and Children who become witnesses to criminal acts.
Letter c What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are in underdeveloped, frontier, and outermost areas in an environment with cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, and religions different from other children, whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.
Letter d What is meant by "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" are Children who become victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.
What is meant by "Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through the Child's sexual organs or other organs of the Child, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecent acts.
Letter e What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.
Letter f What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Pornography" are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.
Letter g What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.
Letter h What is meant by "Child Victims of Kidnapping" are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Selling" are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to other parties for compensation or other reasons.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Trafficking" are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, thereby obtaining consent from a person who holds control over another person, whether conducted within the country or internationally, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.
Letter i What is meant by "Child Victims of Physical Violence" are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Psychological Violence" are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.
Letter j What is meant by "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" are Children who experience forced sexual relations, forced sexual relations in unnatural and/or unwanted ways, and forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
Letter k What is meant by "Child Victims of Terrorism Network" are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by terrorism crimes whether as a Child victim, a Child perpetrator, a Child of a perpetrator, and a Child witness.
Letter l What is meant by "Children with Disabilities" are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
Letter m What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.
Letter n What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.
What is meant by Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm to the Child's growth and development process.
Letter o What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Their Parents' Condition" are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a stigma or bad view from labeling related to their parents' condition.

Article 62 Paragraph (1)
Letter a What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disrupts the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.
Letter b What is meant by "Children in Contact with the Law" are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who become victims of criminal acts, and Children who become witnesses to criminal acts.
Letter c What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are in underdeveloped, frontier, and outermost areas in an environment with cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, and religions different from other children, whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.
Letter d What is meant by "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" are Children who become victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.
What is meant by "Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through the Child's sexual organs or other organs of the Child, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecent acts.
Letter e What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.
Letter f What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Pornography" are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.
Letter g What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.
Letter h What is meant by "Child Victims of Kidnapping" are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Selling" are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to other parties for compensation or other reasons.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Trafficking" are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, thereby obtaining consent from a person who holds control over another person, whether conducted within the country or internationally, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.
Letter i What is meant by "Child Victims of Physical Violence" are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Psychological Violence" are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.
Letter j What is meant by "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" are Children who experience forced sexual relations, forced sexual relations in unnatural and/or unwanted ways, and forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
Letter k What is meant by "Child Victims of Terrorism Network" are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by terrorism crimes whether as a Child victim, a Child perpetrator, a Child of a perpetrator, and a Child witness.
Letter l What is meant by "Children with Disabilities" are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
Letter m What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.
Letter n What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.
What is meant by Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm to the Child's growth and development process.
Letter o What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Their Parents' Condition" are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a stigma or bad view from labeling related to their parents' condition.

Children Requiring Special Protection hereinafter abbreviated as AMPK are Children in emergency situations, Children in conflict with the law, Children from minority and isolated groups, Children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, Children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse, Children who are victims of pornography, Children with HIV/AIDS, Children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, and/or trafficking, Children who are victims of physical and/or psychological violence, Children who are victims of sexual crimes, Children who are victims of terrorist networks, Children with disabilities, Children who are victims of abuse and neglect, Children with deviant social behavior, and Children who are victims of stigmatization from labeling related to their parents' condition, and Children with other problems. 30. Gender Data is data regarding the relationship of relations in status, roles, and conditions between men and women. 31. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of Gender and Child Data consisting of components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/institutions and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of Gender Responsive and child-caring development. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree. 33. Family Quality is the condition of the Family determined by the dimensions of quality of legality and structure, quality of physical resilience, quality of economic resilience, quality of socio-psychological resilience, and quality of socio-cultural resilience in realizing Gender Equality and Child Rights. 34. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and preventing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 35. Violence Against Women hereinafter abbreviated as KTP is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 36. Violence Against Children hereinafter abbreviated as KTA is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom. 37. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household. 38. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life. 39. Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 40. Witness and/or Victim is a witness who is also a victim who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, resulting from the criminal act of human trafficking. 41. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 42. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 43. Business World is micro business, small business, medium business, and large business that conducts economic activities in Indonesia and is domiciled in Indonesia. 44. Community is individuals, families, groups, mass media, business world, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 45. Community Participation is the role of community members to channel their aspirations, thoughts, and interests in the administration of Regional Government. 46. Community Organization hereinafter referred to as Ormas is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities, and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 47. Social Conflict hereinafter referred to as Conflict is a feud and/or physical clash with Violence between two or more community groups that lasts for a certain time and has broad impacts resulting in insecurity and social disintegration thus disrupting national stability and hindering national development. 48. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit formed by the Regional Government in providing services for women and Children who experience Violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 49.

Article 62 Paragraph (1)
Letter a What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disrupts the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.
Letter b What is meant by "Children in Contact with the Law" are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who become victims of criminal acts, and Children who become witnesses to criminal acts.
Letter c What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are in underdeveloped, frontier, and outermost areas in an environment with cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, and religions different from other children, whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.
Letter d What is meant by "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" are Children who become victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.
What is meant by "Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through the Child's sexual organs or other organs of the Child, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecent acts.
Letter e What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.
Letter f What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Pornography" are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.
Letter g What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.
Letter h What is meant by "Child Victims of Kidnapping" are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Selling" are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to other parties for compensation or other reasons.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Trafficking" are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, thereby obtaining consent from a person who holds control over another person, whether conducted within the country or internationally, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.
Letter i What is meant by "Child Victims of Physical Violence" are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Psychological Violence" are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.
Letter j What is meant by "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" are Children who experience forced sexual relations, forced sexual relations in unnatural and/or unwanted ways, and forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
Letter k What is meant by "Child Victims of Terrorism Network" are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by terrorism crimes whether as a Child victim, a Child perpetrator, a Child of a perpetrator, and a Child witness.
Letter l What is meant by "Children with Disabilities" are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
Letter m What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.
Letter n What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.
What is meant by Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm to the Child's growth and development process.
Letter o What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Their Parents' Condition" are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a stigma or bad view from labeling related to their parents' condition.

Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of Gender and Child Data consisting of components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/institutions and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of Gender Responsive and child-caring development. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree. 33. Family Quality is the condition of the Family determined by the dimensions of quality of legality and structure, quality of physical resilience, quality of economic resilience, quality of socio-psychological resilience, and quality of socio-cultural resilience in realizing Gender Equality and Child Rights. 34. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and preventing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 35. Violence Against Women hereinafter abbreviated as KTP is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 36. Violence Against Children hereinafter abbreviated as KTA is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom. 37. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household. 38. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life. 39. Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 40. Witness and/or Victim is a witness who is also a victim who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, resulting from the criminal act of human trafficking. 41. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 42. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 43. Business World is micro business, small business, medium business, and large business that conducts economic activities in Indonesia and is domiciled in Indonesia. 44. Community is individuals, families, groups, mass media, business world, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 45. Community Participation is the role of community members to channel their aspirations, thoughts, and interests in the administration of Regional Government. 46. Community Organization hereinafter referred to as Ormas is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities, and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 47. Social Conflict hereinafter referred to as Conflict is a feud and/or physical clash with Violence between two or more community groups that lasts for a certain time and has broad impacts resulting in insecurity and social disintegration thus disrupting national stability and hindering national development. 48. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit formed by the Regional Government in providing services for women and Children who experience Violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 49.

Article 35
The Regency Regional Government in implementing the protection of women with disabilities as referred to in Article 34, shall:
a. provide information service units and rapid response for women with disabilities who are victims of Violence;
b. provide Special Protection for women with disabilities; and
c. provide accessible safe houses for women with disabilities.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Part One Definitions
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data according to sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and fulfilling their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self, resulting in, or likely to result in, physical, psychological, and sexual harm or suffering to women and children, including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal actions, and other actions to ensure Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, family environment rights and alternative care, basic health rights and welfare, as well as education rights, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Article 51

Article 62 Paragraph (1)
Letter a What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disrupts the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.
Letter b What is meant by "Children in Contact with the Law" are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who become victims of criminal acts, and Children who become witnesses to criminal acts.
Letter c What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are in underdeveloped, frontier, and outermost areas in an environment with cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, and religions different from other children, whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.
Letter d What is meant by "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" are Children who become victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.
What is meant by "Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through the Child's sexual organs or other organs of the Child, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecent acts.
Letter e What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.
Letter f What is meant by "Children Who Become Victims of Pornography" are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.
Letter g What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.
Letter h What is meant by "Child Victims of Kidnapping" are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Selling" are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to other parties for compensation or other reasons.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Trafficking" are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, thereby obtaining consent from a person who holds control over another person, whether conducted within the country or internationally, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.
Letter i What is meant by "Child Victims of Physical Violence" are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.
What is meant by "Child Victims of Psychological Violence" are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.
Letter j What is meant by "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" are Children who experience forced sexual relations, forced sexual relations in unnatural and/or unwanted ways, and forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
Letter k What is meant by "Child Victims of Terrorism Network" are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by terrorism crimes whether as a Child victim, a Child perpetrator, a Child of a perpetrator, and a Child witness.
Letter l What is meant by "Children with Disabilities" are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
Letter m What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.
Letter n What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.
What is meant by Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm to the Child's growth and development process.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Part One Definitions
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data according to sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and fulfilling their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self, resulting in, or likely to result in, physical, psychological, and sexual harm or suffering to women and children, including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal actions, and other actions to ensure Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, family environment rights and alternative care, basic health rights and welfare, as well as education rights, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.
