I. GENERAL
Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in community, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of acts of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.
Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a main pillar in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.
At the level of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Region, is essentially one implementation of the administration of concurrent government affairs which is the authority of the Sumedang Regency Region in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
The Policy on Empowerment and Protection of Women, Child Protection, and Improvement of Family Quality in the Sumedang Regency Region is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Region from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated manner, continuously, and sustainably, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of empowerment and protection of women, child protection, and improvement of family quality.
To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection and to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Region, it must be regulated and stipulated by a Regional Regulation.

Part Two Improvement of Family Quality in Realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas
Article 83 Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas is implemented through:
a. implementation of policies, programs, and activities; and
b. development of materials and implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families.
(1) Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas is implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
(2) Standards for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. institutional arrangements;
b. availability of communication, information, and education materials;
c. synergy and coordination; and
d. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
(3) Procedures for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of:
a. policy advocacy and family assistance to realize Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas include:
1. preparation of planning and budgeting documents for Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
2. coordination and synchronization of policy formulation for Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
3. increasing Community Participation and mass media in improving Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights; and
4. strengthening cooperation of Regency Regional Apparatus to realize Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights.
b. implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families in Regency Areas; and
c. development of Community activities for improving Family Quality in Regency Areas.

CHAPTER VII COOPERATION
Article 96
(1) In order to support the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Administration in the Regency Area, the Regency Regional Government may establish regional cooperation.
(2) Regional cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be conducted by the Regency Regional Government with:
a. other regions;
b. third parties; and/or
c. institutions or regional governments abroad.
(3) Regional cooperation with institutions or regional governments abroad as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c, shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) Regional cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be set forth in a cooperation agreement.
(5) Regional cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented based on laws and regulations governing regional cooperation.

CHAPTER V IMPROVEMENT OF FAMILY QUALITY
Part One General
Article 82 (1) The Regency Regional Government has the authority to organize the Improvement of Family Quality in the Regency Region.
(2) The organization of Improvement of Family Quality in the Regency Region as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in order to support the development of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Regency Region.
(3) The organization of Improvement of Family Quality in the Regency Region as referred to in paragraph (1), is implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus that organizes governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Seventh Part Child-Friendly Regency
Article 81
(1) The Regency Regional Government shall organize KLA in the Regency Region.
(2) The organization of KLA in the Regency Region as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through the integration of policies, programs, and development activities of the Central Government and the Regency Regional Government.
(3) Further provisions regarding the Organization of KLA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a separate Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER XII AWARDS
Article 102
(1) The Regency Regional Government may grant awards to parties who play an active role in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Awards as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of:
a. certificate;
b. trophy; and/or
c. coaching program.
(3) The granting of awards as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the financial capacity of the Regency.

Article 100
(1) The Regency Regional Government may establish an evaluation Team in conducting evaluation of the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) The establishment of the evaluation team as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.
(3) The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.
(4) The results of the evaluation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection shall serve as input material in the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the coming year.
(5) Further provisions regarding monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Regency as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated in a Regent's Regulation.

Part Two Obligations and Responsibilities
Article 51
(1) The Regency Regional Government, the Community, the Family, and Parents or Guardians are obliged and responsible for the administration of Child Protection in the Regency.
(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the Regency Regional Government in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. respecting the fulfillment of Children's Rights without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, group, sex, ethnic origin, culture and language, legal status, birth order, and physical and/or mental condition;
b. implementing and supporting national policies in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency; and
c. providing support for facilities, infrastructure, and the availability of human resources in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency.
(3) The Regency Regional Government, in carrying out its obligations and responsibilities in Child Protection in the Regency as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall do so by:
a. guaranteeing the protection, care, and welfare of Children by taking into account the rights and obligations of Parents, Guardians, or other persons who are legally responsible for Children; and
b. supervising the administration of Child Protection in the Regency.

CHAPTER VI GENDER AND CHILD DATA SYSTEM
Article 95
(1) The Regency Regional Government has the authority to administer the Gender and Child Data System in the Regency Region.
(2) The administration of the Gender and Child Data System in the Regency Region as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in order to support the development of Women's Empowerment and child protection in the Regency Region.
(3) The preparation of the Gender and Child Data System as referred to in paragraph (1) serves as the basis for the preparation of Disaggregated Data related to the conditions and situations of women and men in various development sectors.
(4) Disaggregated Data between women and men as referred to in paragraph (3) must be provided by each Regional Apparatus.
(5) The collection and management of Disaggregated Data is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and is coordinated and published by the Regency Regional Apparatus that carries out governmental affairs in the field of communication and informatics.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree. 33. Family Quality is the condition of the Family determined by the dimensions of quality of legality and structure, quality of physical resilience, quality of economic resilience, quality of socio-psychological resilience, and quality of socio-cultural resilience in realizing Gender Equality and Child Rights. 34. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and preventing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 35. Violence Against Women hereinafter abbreviated as KTP is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 36. Violence Against Children hereinafter abbreviated as KTA is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom. 37. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household. 38. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life. 39. Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 40. Witness and/or Victim is a witness who is also a victim who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, resulting from the criminal act of human trafficking. 41. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 42. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 43. Business World is micro business, small business, medium business, and large business that conducts economic activities in Indonesia and is domiciled in Indonesia. 44. Community is individuals, families, groups, mass media, business world, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 45. Community Participation is the role of community members to channel their aspirations, thoughts, and interests in the administration of Regional Government. 46. Community Organization hereinafter referred to as Ormas is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities, and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 47. Social Conflict hereinafter referred to as Conflict is a feud and/or physical clash with Violence between two or more community groups that lasts for a certain time and has broad impacts resulting in insecurity and social disintegration thus disrupting national stability and hindering national development. 48. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit formed by the Regional Government in providing services for women and Children who experience Violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 49.

I. GENERAL
Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in community, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of acts of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.
Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a main pillar in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.
At the level of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Region, is essentially one implementation of the administration of concurrent government affairs which is the authority of the Sumedang Regency Region in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
The Policy on Empowerment and Protection of Women, Child Protection, and Improvement of Family Quality in the Sumedang Regency Region is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Region from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated manner, continuously, and sustainably, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of empowerment and protection of women, child protection, and improvement of family quality.
To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection and to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Region, it must be regulated and stipulated by a Regional Regulation.

Part Two Improvement of Family Quality in Realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas

a. implementation of policies, programs, and activities; and
b. development of materials and implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families.
(1) Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas is implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
(2) Standards for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. institutional arrangements;
b. availability of communication, information, and education materials;
c. synergy and coordination; and
d. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
(3) Procedures for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of:
a. policy advocacy and family assistance to realize Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas include:
1. preparation of planning and budgeting documents for Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
2. coordination and synchronization of policy formulation for Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
3. increasing Community Participation and mass media in improving Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights; and
4. strengthening cooperation of Regency Regional Apparatus to realize Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights.
b. implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families in Regency Areas; and
c. development of Community activities for improving Family Quality in Regency Areas.

Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and preventing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 35. Violence Against Children hereinafter abbreviated as KTA is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom. 37. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life. 39. Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 40. In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data according to sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and fulfilling their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self, resulting in, or likely to result in, physical, psychological, and sexual harm or suffering to women and children, including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. I. GENERAL
Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in community, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of acts of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.
Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a main pillar in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.
At the level of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Region, is essentially one implementation of the administration of concurrent government affairs which is the authority of the Sumedang Regency Region in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
The Policy on Empowerment and Protection of Women, Child Protection, and Improvement of Family Quality in the Sumedang Regency Region is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Region from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated manner, continuously, and sustainably, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of empowerment and protection of women, child protection, and improvement of family quality.
To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection and to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Region, it must be regulated and stipulated by a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL
Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in community, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of acts of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.
Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a main pillar in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.
At the level of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Region, is essentially one implementation of the administration of concurrent government affairs which is the authority of the Sumedang Regency Region in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
The Policy on Empowerment and Protection of Women, Child Protection, and Improvement of Family Quality in the Sumedang Regency Region is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Region from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated manner, continuously, and sustainably, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of empowerment and protection of women, child protection, and improvement of family quality.
To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection and to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Region, it must be regulated and stipulated by a Regional Regulation.

Part One General
Article 82 (1) The Regency Regional Government has the authority to organize the Improvement of Family Quality in the Regency Region.
(2) The organization of Improvement of Family Quality in the Regency Region as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in order to support the development of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Regency Region.
(3) The organization of Improvement of Family Quality in the Regency Region as referred to in paragraph (1), is implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus that organizes governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Part Two Improvement of Family Quality in Realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas
Article 83 Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas is implemented through:
a. implementation of policies, programs, and activities; and
b. development of materials and implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families.
(1) Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas is implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
(2) Standards for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. institutional arrangements;
b. availability of communication, information, and education materials;
c. synergy and coordination; and
d. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
(3) Procedures for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of:
a. policy advocacy and family assistance to realize Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas include:
1. preparation of planning and budgeting documents for Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
2. coordination and synchronization of policy formulation for Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
3. increasing Community Participation and mass media in improving Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights; and
4. strengthening cooperation of Regency Regional Apparatus to realize Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights.
b. implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families in Regency Areas; and
c. development of Community activities for improving Family Quality in Regency Areas.

CHAPTER VII COOPERATION
Article 96
(1) In order to support the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Administration in the Regency Area, the Regency Regional Government may establish regional cooperation.
(2) Regional cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be conducted by the Regency Regional Government with:
a. other regions;
b. third parties; and/or
c. institutions or regional governments abroad.
(3) Regional cooperation with institutions or regional governments abroad as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c, shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) Regional cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be set forth in a cooperation agreement.
(5) Regional cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented based on laws and regulations governing regional cooperation.

Article 15
(1) The achievement of Women's Empowerment in the fields of politics, law, social, and economy in Community Organizations in Regency Areas as referred to in Article 7 letter c is measured by criteria.
(2) The criteria for Women's Empowerment in the fields of politics, law, social, and economy in Community Organizations in Regency Areas, as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of:
a. the number of Community Organization activities that are synergistic for Women's Empowerment in the fields of politics, law, social, and economy; and
b. the amount of budget contribution from Community Organizations in Regency Areas for Women's Empowerment in the fields of politics, law, social, and economy.

Seventh Part Child-Friendly Regency
Article 81
(1) The Regency Regional Government shall organize KLA in the Regency Region.
(2) The organization of KLA in the Regency Region as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through the integration of policies, programs, and development activities of the Central Government and the Regency Regional Government.
(3) Further provisions regarding the Organization of KLA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a separate Regional Regulation.

Article 100
(1) The Regency Regional Government may establish an evaluation Team in conducting evaluation of the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) The establishment of the evaluation team as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.
(3) The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.
(4) The results of the evaluation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection shall serve as input material in the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the coming year.
(5) Further provisions regarding monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Regency as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated in a Regent's Regulation.

CHAPTER XI REPORTING
Article 101
(1) The Regent compiles and reports the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection to the Governor.
(2) The compilation of reports as referred to in Paragraph (1) is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(3) The reports as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be submitted at least 1 (one) time in 1 (one) year or at any time if necessary.
(4) The implementation of compilation and reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XII AWARDS
Article 102
(1) The Regency Regional Government may grant awards to parties who play an active role in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Awards as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of:
a. certificate;
b. trophy; and/or
c. coaching program.
(3) The granting of awards as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the financial capacity of the Regency.

CHAPTER VI GENDER AND CHILD DATA SYSTEM
Article 95
(1) The Regency Regional Government has the authority to administer the Gender and Child Data System in the Regency Region.
(2) The administration of the Gender and Child Data System in the Regency Region as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in order to support the development of Women's Empowerment and child protection in the Regency Region.
(3) The preparation of the Gender and Child Data System as referred to in paragraph (1) serves as the basis for the preparation of Disaggregated Data related to the conditions and situations of women and men in various development sectors.
(4) Disaggregated Data between women and men as referred to in paragraph (3) must be provided by each Regional Apparatus.
(5) The collection and management of Disaggregated Data is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and is coordinated and published by the Regency Regional Apparatus that carries out governmental affairs in the field of communication and informatics.

Article 58
(1) The strengthening and development of Institutions Providing Services for Improving the Quality of Life of Children in Regency Areas as referred to in Article 53 letter b shall be implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
(2) The standards for strengthening and development of Institutions Providing Services for Improving the Quality of Life of Children in Regency Areas as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) The procedures for strengthening and development as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of:
a. provision of services for improving the quality of life of Children in Regency Areas;
b. coordination and synchronization of the implementation of assistance for improving the quality of life of Children in Regency Areas;
c. development of communication, information, and education on the Fulfillment of Children's Rights for Institutions Providing Services for Improving the Quality of Life of Children in Regency Areas; and
d. strengthening of networks among Institutions Providing Services for Improving the Quality of Life of Children in Regency Areas.
